item.title: Senior Chinese official stresses high-quality development, security in Yunnan
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
KUNMING, Nov. 8 -- Senior Chinese official Wang Xiaohong called for promoting high-quality development based on local conditions while strengthening security measures during an inspection tour of Yunnan Province in southwest China from Saturday to Sunday. Wang, a member of the Secretariat of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and a state councilor, called for fully and faithfully applying the new development philosophy, coordinating development and security, and improving the precision and effectiveness of policy measures to advance high-quality development in light of local conditions. He demanded tough action against prominent illegal activities, including online gambling, telecom fraud, drug-related crimes and smuggling, while stressing the use of technology to strengthen border management and control. Wang visited Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Prefecture and the provincial capital Kunming, where he toured border ports, enterprises, industrial parks and public security checkpoints. Wang urged Yunnan to actively participate in high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and focus on its development into a gateway to South and Southeast Asia. He called for measures to improve the capacity and efficiency of passenger and cargo clearance at border ports, advance the high-quality development of pilot free trade zones, strengthen major transport corridors and promote economic growth in border areas. Wang also emphasized the need to capitalize on the province's comparative advantages by developing distinctive industries, including tourism, culture and flower cultivation, and called for stronger innovation-driven development.

item.title: Xi congratulates Iotova on election as Bulgarian president
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
BEIJING, Nov. 9 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has extended congratulations to Iliana Iotova on her election as president of Bulgaria. In a message on Friday, Xi noted that Bulgaria was the second country in the world to establish diplomatic ties with the People's Republic of China, and that mutual respect, equality, and mutual benefit and win-win results have been hallmarks of the bilateral relations. In recent years, the two countries have been steadily advancing exchanges and cooperation at all levels and across all fields, while their strategic partnership has continued to deepen, said Xi. Xi also said that he attaches great importance to the development of the China-Bulgaria ties. He pledged to work with Iotova to guide the two countries as they march together along their respective paths to development and revitalization, build an even more positive, practical and dynamic bilateral relationship, and thereby bring greater benefits to the two peoples.

item.title: How Xi steers China's green transformation and global climate action
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
BEIJING, Nov. 9 -- In 2026, the intensifying fallout of global climate change -- manifesting in catastrophic flooding, rampant wildfires, and record heatwaves -- reaffirms the imperative for immediate, coordinated global action. With global climate tipping points looming, the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), set to kick off on Monday in Antalya, Türkiye, will offer a new opportunity for the international community to renew momentum for more effective global climate cooperation. Under the leadership of President Xi Jinping, China has over the years stayed committed to advancing ecological protection and green transition domestically, and promoting international climate cooperation, making major global contributions to the world's fight against what many regard as an existential threat to humanity. "LIKE WE PROTECT OUR EYES" "We should protect the environment like we protect our eyes." This evocative principle -- voiced on various occasions by Xi -- frames ecological conservation not merely as a policy choice, but as a vital imperative drawn directly from his own experiences. "Over four decades ago, I lived and worked for many years in a small village on the Loess Plateau in western China," Xi recalled in reply to a letter from student representatives of the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate in 2020. Back then, the ecology and environment there was seriously damaged due to over-development, and the local people were trapped in poverty as a result. That experience has taught him that man and nature are a community of life and that the damage done to nature will ultimately hurt humanity. An avid reader of Chinese classics, Xi has also been deeply influenced by the traditional Chinese philosophy that views man as an integral part of nature. "All beings flourish when they live in harmony and receive nourishment from nature," he has said. This conviction underpins the signature environmental doctrine that "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets," which Xi first introduced in 2005 while serving as Party chief of east China's Zhejiang Province. Upon becoming General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee in 2012, Xi made ecological conservation a national priority. For Xi, ecological conservation requires not only a profound shift in development philosophy, but also robust institutional safeguards. As he has put it, "Eco-environmental protection relies on laws and regulations." At his direction, environmental performance has become a key criterion for evaluating officials, while environmental inspections have reinforced local governments' accountability for fulfilling their environmental responsibilities. Together, these measures have helped steer China's economic growth toward a more resource-efficient and sustainable path. Since 2012, China has sustained a 6 percent average annual economic growth rate while capping an average energy consumption increase to just 3.3 percent. This structural decoupling yielded a 26.1 percent cumulative decline in energy intensity, marking one of the steepest efficiency gains globally. Xi has also led by example in promoting environmental protection and green development. Since becoming China's top leader, he has personally participated in tree-planting activities in Beijing for 14 consecutive years. Forests have the capacity to conserve water, bring in economic benefits, and boost grain production, and now serve well as a carbon sink, he has noted. Today, China has expanded its forest coverage to over 25 percent of its land area, planting trees across an area roughly 1.7 times the size of California since 2012. The annual carbon-sink capacity of China's forests and grassland has exceeded 1.2 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalents. Fuad Gani, vice director of the Graduate School of Sustainable Development at the University of Indonesia, said that China's ecological conservation philosophy stands out for its ability to translate environmental goals into long-term policies and governance frameworks. "It is one of China's most valuable contributions to advancing green transformation on the global stage," he said. "SOMETHING WE MUST DO OURSELVES" Balancing economic growth with green development remains a challenge for economies worldwide, especially emerging markets seeking to meet development needs while pursuing environmental sustainability. In Xi's view, economic growth and the green transition are not opposing forces, but complementary goals. This philosophy is captured in his defining doctrine -- "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets." Achieving China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, Xi has stressed, "is not something that others ask us to do, but something we must do ourselves." Under his leadership, China has effectively aligned emissions reduction with technological innovation, industrial upgrading and energy security, turning the green transition into an increasingly important driver of high-quality development. As early as 2014, when conventional gasoline-powered vehicles still dominated China's roads, Xi recognized the enormous potential of new energy vehicles (NEVs). During an inspection tour of SAIC Motor, a major Chinese carmaker, Xi depicted developing NEVs as the only way for China to move from a major automobile country to an automobile powerhouse. In the following decade, the president has demonstrated consistent support for electric cars, visiting automotive companies, touring laboratories, and showing great interest in trying new home-developed models. China's NEV industry has since grown rapidly, emerging as a flagship of the country's technology-intensive manufacturing sector. Beyond the NEV sector, China has also built the world's largest and most comprehensive clean energy industrial chain, with green and low-carbon industries emerging as an important engine of economic growth. The growing exports of the "new three" -- photovoltaic products, lithium-ion batteries and electric vehicles -- are a testament to China's successful shift toward innovation-driven manufacturing. Beyond its own borders, China is now channeling this green innovation momentum into regional cooperation. China will continue to work with fellow Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) countries to increase the installed capacity of photovoltaic and wind power each by 10 million kilowatts, and nurture more green industry talents through China-SCO cooperation, said Xi at the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the SCO this September. China's exports of solar panels, wind turbines, electric vehicles and batteries this year will help the world to avoid 450 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions, according to a recent analysis by the Finland-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air. The development exemplifies China's strategic push to cultivate "new quality productive forces" -- a policy concept first articulated by Xi in 2023 to drive high-tech innovation and sustainable economic modernization. "Green development," as Xi once put it, "is the defining feature of high-quality development, and new quality productive forces are green in nature." China has turned the challenges of addressing climate change into opportunities for technological innovation, industrial upgrading and high-quality economic development, said Wang Lei, a professor at the School of Government of Beijing Normal University. "Guided by the goals of reducing carbon emissions and strengthening climate resilience, the country has leveraged policy guidance, market incentives and open innovation to drive the transformation of energy, industry, transportation and construction," he added. "EXTREME RESOLUTIONS" Deeply committed to joining world nations to build a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi has repeatedly called on the international community to strengthen cooperation in addressing climate change and actively advanced the building of a fair and equitable global climate governance system for win-win cooperation. "Supreme resources spring from extreme resolutions," Xi said, invoking a perceptive line from French writer Victor Hugo's Les Miserables during his address to the historic 2015 Paris climate change conference. During the summit, Xi put forward important ideas and proposals and worked actively to build consensus among parties, making an indispensable contribution to the eventual adoption of the Paris Agreement. At a special ceremony on Sept. 3, 2016, Xi solemnly handed over China's instrument of joining the Paris Agreement to then UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon. "Had not been President Xi Jinping's initiative, we would not have the Paris Agreement on climate change even now," Ban said in a 2021 interview with Xinhua. In response to the grave challenge of climate change, China has taken on its international responsibilities with what Xi described as "extreme resolutions." At a virtual UN gathering in 2020, Xi announced that China would strive to peak carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060. In 2021, he pledged that China would not build new coal-fired power projects abroad. In recent years, some developed countries, particularly those in the West, have backtracked on their climate commitments, undermining global climate governance. Against this backdrop, Xi announced China's 2035 Nationally Determined Contributions in 2025, including a commitment to reduce economy-wide net greenhouse gas emissions by 7-10 percent from peak levels and to raise the share of non-fossil fuels in total energy consumption to more than 30 percent by 2035. For the first time, China committed to absolute emissions reduction targets covering all economic sectors and all greenhouse gases, providing much-needed certainty and stability for global climate governance. Xi has also emphasized the need to uphold fairness and equity and fully respect developing countries' right to development as the world pursues a green transition. "The transition should serve to narrow rather than widen the North-South gap," he said, urging developed countries to take the lead in fulfilling emissions reduction obligations and provide more financial and technological support to developing countries. Under Xi's leadership, China has been striving to strengthen South-South cooperation on climate change. Xi has proposed the establishment of the Belt and Road Initiative International Green Development Coalition and advocated building a green BRICS partnership. Through these target-driven initiatives, China seeks to deepen cooperation in clean energy, green technology and green industrial development, while helping developing countries strengthen their capacity to address climate change. "The Earth is our one and only home," Xi has said. "To scale up efforts to address climate change and promote sustainable development bears on the future of humanity."

item.title: Chinese premier chairs State Council executive meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
BEIJING, Nov. 6 -- A State Council executive meeting presided over by Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Friday called for strengthening confidence and stepping up policy implementation to ensure China fulfils its major economic and social development targets for the year. The meeting urged faster progress on the construction and implementation of major projects and the country's "six networks" of infrastructure, covering water, power, computing, communications, urban underground pipelines and logistics networks. It called for supporting enterprises in expanding investment in equipment upgrades and intangible assets, and strengthening links of consumption between online and offline markets, as well as urban and rural markets, to foster a virtuous cycle between investment and consumption. The meeting called for making full use of various policy funds, ensuring timely and full disbursement of payments to primary-level authorities and enterprises, and better coordinating fiscal and financial policies in boosting domestic demand. It stressed the need to keep employment stable, prevent risks and safeguard people's livelihoods, calling for stronger employment services for key groups and employment assistance for graduates in difficulty. The meeting urged intensified efforts to identify and address workplace safety risks to prevent major accidents, as well as continued efforts to defuse risks related to local government debt and small and medium-sized financial institutions. It called for improving mechanisms to stabilize the capital market, enhancing the stock market's inherent stability and promoting the stable and sound development of the capital market. The meeting stressed the importance of studying economic priorities for next year and strengthening policy coordination across years to sustain positive economic momentum. The meeting also heard a report on social assistance work, and called for further improvement to the social assistance system, noting that social assistance is an important institutional arrangement for ensuring a basic safety net for people's livelihoods. It underlined the significance of expanding the scope of social assistance to meet new needs and strengthening recipients' intrinsic motivation for self-development, while urging efforts to promote service-based social assistance, such as caregiving and other forms of support, to give people in need a greater sense of gain.

item.title: Chinese vice premier to chair second China-Canada economic, financial strategic dialogue in Canada
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 6 -- As agreed between China and Canada, the second China-Canada Economic and Financial Strategic Dialogue will be held in Canada on November 9, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Friday. He Lifeng, member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council, will co-chair the dialogue as the Chinese lead person with the co-leaders on the Canadian side, the spokesperson said. The Canadian co-leaders are Minister of Finance and National Revenue Francois-Philippe Champagne and Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu, according to the spokesperson.

item.title: Chinese vice premier calls for joint efforts to achieve balanced trade
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Chinese vice premier calls for joint efforts to achieve balanced trade Updated: November 6, 2026 08:19Xinhua SHANGHAI, Nov. 5 -- Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang on Thursday called for joint efforts to achieve balanced trade through greater market openness, deeper investment cooperation, innovation, and the removal of trade barriers. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks in his keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the ninth China International Import Expo and the Hongqiao International Economic Forum in Shanghai. Noting that profound changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, Ding said economic globalization is facing headwinds, imbalances in global development remain prominent, and the international economic and trade order is being severely impacted. Concerns over trade imbalances are understandable, and the key is how to achieve balanced trade, he said. He called on countries to share market opportunities, enhance openness and connectivity, better leverage their respective comparative advantages, and promote balance by making the economic pie bigger together. He also urged deeper investment cooperation and efforts to optimize the cross-border layout of industries, create favorable conditions for businesses, and promote balance through integration into global industrial and supply chains. Ding stressed the need to harness innovation, improve supply quality, expand the frontiers of trade, and promote balance through advancing transformation and upgrading. He also called for greater mutual understanding and trust, giving due consideration to each other's legitimate concerns, resolving differences through consultation, and promoting balance by removing barriers.

item.title: Xi votes in local legislative election in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 6 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping cast his ballot at a polling station in Beijing on Friday to elect deputies to a local people's congress. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, voted at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress. Xi stressed efforts to practice whole-process people's democracy, uphold Party leadership, and strengthen oversight throughout the election process to ensure that deputies who meet the people's expectations are elected. Around 3:30 p.m. Friday, Xi arrived at the polling station, gave his voter registration card to staff for verification, and got a ballot. He cast his ballot after filling it. Noting that the election of deputies to people's congresses is an important foundation for upholding, improving and practicing the people's congress system, Xi underlined the need to give full play to democracy, strictly act in accordance with the law, and ensure that the election is carried out fairly and cleanly. On Friday afternoon, other senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi cast their ballots in person, while Han Zheng entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Former Chinese leader Hu Jintao also entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Friday saw people vote at 13,054 polling stations across Beijing to elect 4,898 new deputies to the people's congresses at the district level and 11,137 deputies to the township-level people's congresses.
